q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis

## (a) Time left until resolution
Today is August 20, 2026. The Q2 FY2027 earnings release is scheduled for August 26, 2026. That's **6 days** until the announcement.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

The question asks specifically for NVIDIA's **forward guidance** (not actual Q2 results) that will be announced on August 26, 2026.

Key facts from the research:
- Q1 FY2027 forward guidance (given May 20, 2026): $91.0 billion ±2% for Q2
- This means Q1 FY2027 guidance ranged from $89.18B to $92.82B
- Q2 FY2027 actual results are being reported on August 26, 2026
- At that time, NVIDIA will also provide guidance for Q3 FY2027 (the next quarter)
- Analyst expectations for Q2 actual revenue: $91B-$95B range
- BofA Securities (August 10): $94B-$95B estimate

The most likely outcome is that NVIDIA's **forward guidance for Q3 FY2027** (to be given with Q2 results) will reflect:
1. Strong demand continuation in data center/AI
2. Historical pattern of NVIDIA beating guidance and raising outlooks
3. Analyst consensus clustering around $93.5B-$95B for Q2 actuals
4. Forward guidance typically conservative but stronger than prior quarter guidance when beat

Given NVIDIA's historical pattern of strong AI demand growth, and that the previous forward guidance of $91B appears likely to be beaten (analyst consensus $93.5B-$95B), the Q3 FY2027 guidance will likely be raised materially.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- Unexpected supply chain disruptions or yield issues
- China export restrictions tightening unexpectedly
- Weaker-than-expected enterprise AI capex spending
- Competitive pressures from AMD or other rivals accelerating
- Macro slowdown signals reducing customer capex confidence
- Conservative guidance (below actual Q2 results) to set easy targets

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- Continued acceleration of AI/data center demand
- Better-than-expected Q2 actual results (currently $94B-$95B consensus)
- Strong pre-order/booking signals for Q3
- Winning new major cloud customer deployments
- International expansion (EU, Asia) accelerating
- Gross margin expansion reducing pressure on unit growth
- Raising guidance significantly above Q2 actual results (historical pattern)

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

The research provides:
- Q1 FY2027 forward guidance: $91.0B ±2%
- Q2 FY2027 analyst consensus actual revenue: $91B-$95B range, with BofA at $94B-$95B

No explicit historical base rate data is provided in the background or research for how much NVIDIA typically raises guidance quarter-to-quarter. However, the pattern described (beating $91B guidance with $94B-$95B actuals) suggests forward guidance for Q3 would likely be **above the Q2 actual results**, consistent with NVIDIA's historical practice of conservative guidance.

The range provided is 99.5B to 115.5B, which brackets plausible forward guidance values.

## Reasoning toward the point estimate

**Key insight**: The question asks for forward guidance (Q3 FY2027), not actual Q2 results.

Given:
- Q2 expected actual results: $93.5B-$95B consensus
- Historical pattern: NVIDIA raises guidance after beating
- Typical guidance safety margin: 2-5% above current guidance
- Strong demand environment continues

A reasonable forward guidance for Q3 FY2027 would be:
- Conservative approach: $95B-$97B (beating Q2 likely actual by modest amount)
- Base case: $98B-$102B (reflecting continued growth momentum)
- Bullish case: $103B-$107B (more aggressive if Q2 beats significantly)

The midpoint of the range provided (99.5 to 115.5) is 107.5B, suggesting the question anticipates materially higher guidance.

My estimate anchors on:
- Q2 actual likely ~$94.5B (midpoint of consensus)
- Sequential growth guidance typically 5-8% for NVIDIA in strong periods
- This suggests Q3 guidance around $99B-$102B
- But given the strong momentum and typically conservative guidance practice, $100B-$105B is reasonable

**Point estimate**: 101.5 billion dollars (slightly above $100B, reflecting solid sequential growth from expected Q2 actuals)

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue was $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%, according to its Q1 FY2027 earnings release on May 20, 2026 [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm). This guidance explicitly excludes any Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html), [news.ifyouspent.com](https://news.ifyouspent.com/en/news/nvidia-earnings-what-to-watch-august-2026), [techbloat.com](https://www.techbloat.com/nvidia-earnings-preview-another-revenue-record-is-in-sight-but-profit-growth-could-slow.html). The midpoint of $91.0 billion is above the average analyst estimate of $86.84 billion at the time [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html).

NVIDIA's Q2 FY2027 earnings release is scheduled for August 26, 2026 [news.ifyouspent.com](https://news.ifyouspent.com/en/news/nvidia-earnings-what-to-watch-august-2026), [techbloat.com](https://www.techbloat.com/nvidia-earnings-preview-another-revenue-record-is-in-sight-but-profit-growth-could-slow.html). Analysts are expecting revenue near $91 billion, with some aggregators pegging it closer to $93.5 billion [news.ifyouspent.com](https://news.ifyouspent.com/en/news/nvidia-earnings-what-to-watch-august-2026). A BofA Securities preview from August 10, for instance, estimated Q2 revenue around $94 billion to $95 billion [techbloat.com](https://www.techbloat.com/nvidia-earnings-preview-another-revenue-record-is-in-sight-but-profit-growth-could-slow.html).
